result:
There is a strange, suspended reality to an airport terminal at three in the morning. Outside, the tarmac glistens under amber floodlights, a vast concrete ocean where giant metal birds sleep between voyages. Inside, time loses its grip. The usual frantic river of rolling suitcases and hurried footsteps has dried up, leaving behind a quiet sediment of stranded travelers and night-shift workers.

The carpet, patterned in chaotic geometry designed to hide coffee stains, absorbs the low hum of a distant floor buffer. A solitary man in a wrinkled business suit sleeps upright across two unforgiving plastic chairs, his briefcase clutched to his chest like a teddy bear. Fifty feet away, a backpacker uses a rolled-up fleece as a pillow, sprawling on the linoleum near a cluster of coveted power outlets. At this hour, exhaustion is the great equalizer.

A metallic voice chimes over the intercom, reminding no one in particular not to leave baggage unattended. The smell of burnt espresso drifts from a lone open kiosk, mingling with the sterile scent of lemon floor cleaner. 

In this liminal space, you are neither where you came from nor where you are going. You are simply in between. Your past is packed tightly into a carry-on bag, and your future hasn't yet been cleared for takeoff. As the first bruised purples of dawn begin to bleed into the eastern sky beyond the control tower, the terminal takes a collective breath, preparing to wake up and remember that time exists after all.
